title: The Distinction Between Human and Divine Thought
english: And indeed these manias are not false; for instance, those receiving God or those receiving Christ are god-bearers, and these manias are not false but true, instead of being 'repressed.' For if they were not also true manias, he would not have said: 'he who has had a false hope regarding madness' (1 Cor 6:9). Those according to the Phrygians, not having been ignorant of how these things are said, taking both the meaning of madness and of ecstasy, call the spirit-bearing men as having spoken in ecstasy or having prophesied. And they speak truly regarding ecstasy, but not regarding derangement or insanity.

If indeed Paul says: 'whether we have gone out of our minds, [it is] to God' (1 Cor 6:9), he is not speaking of madness, but of standing outside of human [limits] and... [gap]... having given. And this word is also said regarding wonder: 'And after these things the sons of Israel will turn back and will seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they will be astonished at the Lord and in His good things' (Ps 142:7). He signifies wonder here.

'You have done many things, Lord my God, Your wonders' (Ps 142:5). Having been tested by the doing of the things spoken, since he did not only enjoy these good things, but—so that I may say this—was drawn to these from childhood—and so indeed His anointing while being a child has happened paradoxically, and he says: 'You have done many things, Lord my God, Your wonders.' Many and great things are, 'and with Your thoughts' (Ps 142:4), according to which You do wonders, 'no one shall be like [You].' No one is able to do such wonders; no one is able to bring someone out of the pit of misery and from the mud of matter and set his feet upon a rock and direct his steps and the other things.

The 'there is no one who shall be like' if said in reference to the Father, does not speak concerning the Son; for none of the begotten shall be like [the Father]. But the Son is not [to be] compared; for He is eternal, the icon and character of the divine essence. There is not...

Having the future of becoming like [Him]; for he is like. Regarding: the 'thoughts'? Thoughts are primarily called the thoughts concerning each individual thing. Just as the act of reasoning is a conversation of the soul, and it is not possible to say many things at once, so also the thoughts concerning each individual thing are called thoughts.

A logical place is given for asking whether knowing is the same as reasoning, and it has been said that they are not the same; for there are many things known without reasoning, and many things reasoned about without being known, so that knowing is not the same as reasoning. One is able to grasp a concept of a whole genus and of a whole species. But to know each individual thing, each being reasoned about by itself, it is not possible to do all at once. Regarding: so that the reasoning is upon sensation? But it is upon the individual things being reasoned about. Just as it is not possible to say many things at once while knowing many things, since the intellect is a kind of speech of the soul, it is not possible to reason about many things at once.

God, therefore, has such thoughts that He knows all things at once, yet in a different way than men; for in Isaiah He said: 'As the heavens are far from the earth, so are your thoughts from my thought' (Isaiah 55:9). He wished to show the superiority of His own intellect through a sensory example; for His intellect has not stayed away from the intellect of men locally, but by a greatness of superiority. And with your thoughts no one shall be like. No one is like the thoughts of God. Just as you would say: 'No one shall be like the creation of God.'

For even if they were creators among men, they do not construct the underlying matter of the things coming into being. For example, if a craftsman makes a bed or a throne, he does not make the wood by his art. He only imposes the end upon the previously taken matter. But God, not finding matter, imposes the form upon it, but rather composes it with the form. I have declared and I have spoken, they were multiplied beyond...
